narration:
Tidemark does not build against water; it builds around it, the way a ledger is built around a debt. You come down into Saltmarrow Crossing on the low road, where the causeway stones sit a hand's width above the tide and the stalls on either side stand on stilts gone green to the knee. The air tastes of salt and wet rope and someone's frying fish. Everywhere there is counting — coin, crates, days of passage, the small ceaseless arithmetic of a kingdom that believes in nothing but flow. Nobody looks twice at the ash-grey cast of your skin or the way the dust of your lineage never quite washes out of the creases of your hands. This is a crossing place. Everyone here is from somewhere that isn't here.

You feel it before you understand it: the thing behind your ribs that has lived there since the creek, since the cold, since your brother's hand going slack in water you had *measured*. It does not speak. It tallies. The tide is rising four fingers faster than the tide-bell allows for, because the wind has turned and the bell does not know about wind. There are nine travelers packed onto the Low Causeway waiting for the tollgate to lift — a woman with a hand-cart of salted eel, two Stonewarden drovers, a Feral boy asleep on a crate, a Vaelwyn in a good coat who keeps checking a pocket-watch as if time were the problem. Sixty paces of open stone to the far quay. At the pace the crowd will move once the gate lifts, four of them make it dry. Three make it wet. Two do not make it. You know which two. The knowing arrives complete, unasked for, and utterly certain — and the old cruelty of it settles in your gut, because being right has never once been the same as being able to help.

The tide-clerk in the booth — a thin woman with ink to the elbow, brass plate at her collar reading HESPER QUILL, TIDE-CLERK, THIRD SEAL — raises her hand to the gate-chain. She has not looked at the water in some minutes. Down the causeway, the boy on the crate stirs; the eel-cart woman shifts her grip; somewhere under the stilts the sea makes a sound like a held breath being let out slowly. You have perhaps twenty seconds before the chain comes up, the crowd surges, and your arithmetic begins collecting. Speak to the clerk, and you spend the seconds you'd need to move. Move, and you can reach exactly one of the two. Say nothing, and the ledger simply balances itself, as it always has, without your permission.

What do you do?

world_events.scene_summary: Kaelen Vurr arrives at a stilt-built market crossing in Tidemark just as a wind-driven tide outpaces the tide-bell. Nine travelers wait behind a tollgate for a sixty-pace run of open causeway; Ledger of the Drowned has already told Kaelen, with total certainty, that two of them will not make it, and that he can reach at most one.

new_entities.name: Saltmarrow Crossing
new_entities.description: A stilt-built Tidemark market and tollgate on the Low Causeway, where passage depends on a tide-bell that does not account for wind.

new_entities.name: Hesper Quill
new_entities.description: Tide-clerk of Saltmarrow Crossing, Third Seal — ink-stained, procedural, trusts the tide-bell over her own eyes.

narrative_memory_updates.note: Kaelen arrived at Saltmarrow Crossing and immediately foresaw two deaths on the Low Causeway with only enough time to intervene for one.

gm_note: Note: 'Ashborn' is not one of Vaeltharion's nine canonical races.
